case_name: State of Madhya Pradesh v Basanti Lal
respondent:
Basanti Lal
Supreme Court of India

Cr.A. No.772 Of 1996
The Order of the Court was as follows:

The respondent along with six other persons were charged for an offence punishable u/s. 302 IPC read with S. 149 IPC for having committed the murder of one Sajjan Singh at about 10 p.m. of 30th June, 1983 in Panth Piploda village within the jurisdiction of police station Tal. The incident in question took place when the deceased had gone to ease himself. It is also the case of the prosecution that at that time the mother of the respondent was present there who was examined as PW.1.

facts: The respondent along with six other persons were charged for an offence punishable u/s. 302 IPC read with S. 149 IPC for having committed the murder of one Sajjan Singh at about 10 p.m. of 30th June, 1983 in Panth Piploda village within the jurisdiction of police station Tal.
The prosecution alleges that the respondent herein had fired shots at the deceased causing chest injury while other accused persons were armed with lathis though they did not take part in the attack.

The trial court after going through the material on record came to the conclusion that the prosecution has established its case against the respondent herein only while against the other accused persons it is failed to do so, accordingly, acquitted those persons and convicted the respondent herein for the offence punishable u/s. 302 IPC.
The High Court during the course of re-appreciation of the evidence noted the following findings for not accepting the prosecution case:
Having heard arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and after having perused the records we find no reason to disagree with the High Court, therefore, we find no merit in this appeal.
court_reasoning: we find no reason to disagree with the High Court
therefore, we find no merit in this appeal
holding: The appeal fails and the same is dismissed.
